text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former police commissioner, now a prison inmate after being sentenced over involvement in the death of a man under arrest, inspects school to be used as correctional facility. Lawrence Pullicino accompanied prison authorities on tour of a former school being turned into an extension of the prisons.
- Bar owner defies gun-wielding robber, hurling bottles of water at him and making him flee.
- Fares on helicopter service linking Malta to island of Gozo expected to rise steeply. The service has been making losses for the past three years.
- Prime Minister Alfred Sant, visiting tourism exhibition, says he notes sense of optimism among tour operators. Tourism dropped six percent last year.

- Two police inspectors visit Greece as part of inquiry into disappearance of a Maltese launch on Christmas day. The launch is alleged to have been involved in the drowning of some 300 would-be illegal immigrants between Malta and Sicily. No wreckage or bodies were ever found.
